title: Sunlight firm sails into Chinese market with marine battery deal – Batteries International
content:
Energy Storage, Lithium, News
Read Later
Aesen 116H integrates hybrid propulsion and energy storage systems
The Lehmann Marine battery systems subsidiary of Greece-based lead and lithium battery major, the Sunlight Group, has entered the Chinese market with a commercial partnership.
Sunlight said on October 5 Lehmann had secured its first Asian deployment with the commissioning of its modular CUBE battery system aboard the state-of-the-art hybrid fast crew boat Aesen 116H.
The 42-metre vessel was built in China by Cheoy Lee Shipyards for Singapore-based Aesen. By integrating hybrid propulsion and energy storage systems, Aesen 116H is engineered to optimise engine loading and power utilisation, enabling an estimated 30%-40% reduction in fuel consumption compared with conventionally powered crew boats operating under similar duty cycles
The China deal comes just weeks after Sunlight
announced
the launch of full operations at the 300MWh per annum capacity battery production line for Lehmann at its Xanthi plant in Greece.
Sunlight CEO Lampros Bisalas said: “Growing demand in Asia for European expertise, innovation, and service throughout the battery lifecycle, opens up significant prospects for a Greek industrial group with a global reach, making this specific partnership a springboard for our further commercial growth in the Asia-Pacific region.”
Sunlight
acquired
a 51% stake in Lehmann in a “multi-million euro” deal in 2025.
At the heart of Lehmann’s existing product portfolio are two battery systems ― CUBE and AQUBE. CUBE, introduced in 2023, is an air-cooled LFP system with patented cooling technology and a modular, flexible architecture. AQUBE is the firm’s next-generation water-cooled LFP system, which is the successor to Lehmann’s original water-cooled COBRA.

title: New high forecast for global lead metal surplus in 2027  – Batteries International
content: The global supply of refined lead metal is forecast to soar to 163kt in 2027, according to latest data from the Lisbon-based International Lead and Zinc Study Group (ILZSG). Worldwide supply of refined lead metal is already expected by the group to exceed demand by 90kt by the end of 2026. ILZSG’s latest forecasts were presented at the organisation’s attendees at its  71st two-day session on October 15-16. Global demand for refined lead metal is forecast to increase by 0.9% to 13.79 million tonnes this year and by 1% to 13.92 million tonnes in 2027. In China, despite stable demand from the replacement battery market, declines in both lead acid battery exports and vehicle production will limit growth in lead usage to only 0.2% in 2026, according to the group. European demand is expected to increase by 1.3% in 2026, mainly due to rises in apparent usage (production + imports-exports + stock) in Germany, Greece, Poland, Slovenia and Spain, which will more than offset declines in France and the UK. Usage is also forecast to rise in Brazil, India, Indonesia, Mexico and the US, but to decrease in South Korea and Turkey. Meanwhile, world lead mine supply is forecast to fall by 2.8% to 4.44 million tonnes in 2026. Production is expected to recover by 2.9% to 4.58 million tonnes in 2027. ILZSG said a similar trend is anticipated in China, where output is forecast to decline by 1% in 2026, followed by a significant recovery of more than 4% in 2027. In 2026, refined lead output is expected to increase in India, South Korea, Turkey and Brazil, where new secondary capacity was commissioned in 2025. However, ILZSG said these increases will be partially offset by a reduction in China. In 2027, metal supply is forecast to continue to rise in India and South Korea, to recover in China, but to decline marginally in Europe. Batteries International reported a warning by Tianneng Power International earlier this year of a potential half-year profit fall of up to 66% as high raw material costs hit its mainstay lead acid battery business. However, the China-based lead battery major, part of the Tianneng Group, said long-term prospects were strong. title: Peak Energy hails $108m capital boost for sodium ion battery storage plans – Batteries International
content: Sodium ion ESS developer Peak Energy has announced a $108 million capital boost after closing an oversubscribed Series ‘B’ financing round led by General Motors (GM). The funding round, confirmed on October 21, was supported by other companies including LG Technology Ventures — and will help Peak fulfil over $1 billion in existing orders and launch its ESS into the data centre market. Peak said earlier this year it would build a 4GWh Na ion BESS manufacturing plant in Sacramento, California, with a capital investment of up to $71 million. The battery developer has an existing partnership with GM to jointly develop next generation Na ion battery cells for the storage market. Peak says its flagship passively cooled ESS is engineered to address the components that make energy storage expensive to operate and maintain. The company claims its “fundamentally simpler architecture” can reduce the cost of energy by up to 20% compared with conventional storage systems. In addition, Peak’s system claims to emit virtually no noise, consume no water and eliminates the leading causes of battery fires. The new capital boost will supercharge Peak’s ability to scale and deliver as the world increasingly turns to passively cooled Na ion storage to meet energy needs, co-founder and CEO Landon Mossburg said. GM Ventures president Kevin McCabe said the auto giant’s corporate venture capital arm was investing “to help Peak Energy continue to scale this innovative technology because we believe it has significant potential in the energy storage market as a safe, cost-effective solution using abundant, domestically sourced materials”. title: Korea supreme court upholds jail sentences over fatal battery factory fire – Batteries International
content: South Korea’s supreme court has upheld a four-year prison sentence for the CEO of a battery manufacturer where a factory fire in 2024 killed 23 employees and injured nine others. A district court initially sentenced both Park Soon-kwan, CEO of primary lithium battery firm Aricell and his senior executive son, Park Joong-un, to 15 years in prison following the fire at the plant in Hwaseong, 45km south of Seoul. Their sentences were cut to four and seven years, respectively, by an appeals court, after some charges were overturned and compensation settlements with bereaved families were taken into account. On October 20, the supreme court upheld the appeals court rulings, including a fine of KRW1 million ($750) for Park Joong-un. The court also upheld a KRW800 million corporate fine against Aricell. The appeals court had previously cleared Park and his son of a key charge that they failed to install an emergency exit on the factory’s second floor. In explaining its decision, the appeals court said safety rules did not specifically require exits on every floor. According to the supreme court’s ruling, seen by Batteries International , some of those caught up in the fire included foreigners working illegally. At the time of the fire, the Aricell factory housed an estimated 35,000 battery cells on its second floor, where batteries were inspected and packaged. The supreme court said there had been a failure to manage potential overheating of batteries at all stages after electrolyte injection and vital equipment such as heat and gas detectors were not installed. Aricell’s risk assessment procedures failed to adequately account for the specific hazards of manufacturing batteries using lithium, which poses an explosion risk, the supreme court said. title: VW America recalls nearly 23,000 SUV models over battery fire risk – Batteries International
content: Volkswagen Group of America is recalling nearly 23,000 of its ID.4 electric SUVs, warning of a fire risk linked to a potential defect in the model’s high-voltage battery pack. The US National Highway Traffic Safety Administration (NHTSA) said the recall, which follows others by the automaker earlier this year, warned the high voltage battery in affected vehicles may fail and lead to a fire. The NHTSA confirmed on October 6 the latest recall includes model year 2023-2026 ID.4s produced between January 1, 2023 and February 1, 2025. However, VW estimates just 0.1% of recalled vehicles have the battery defect, the agency said. According to VW specifications, the ID.4 SUV uses NMC as the primary battery chemistry, with tech supplied by various battery manufacturers. Vehicle owners are advised to only charge their vehicles to a maximum of 80% battery capacity until a repair has been completed. Alex Ansley, chief of NHTSA’s recall management division office of defects investigation enforcement, said: “The remedy is currently under development. Interim letters notifying owners of the safety risk are expected to be mailed November 27, 2026.” VW Group of America has already recalled more than 44,000 model year 2023-2025 ID.4 electric SUVs for the risk of battery fires across two separate recalls — notified to the NHTSA in January 2026. That followed another in December 2025 for 629 ID.4s that were also linked to the risk of battery fire. title: Redwood Materials expands battery recycling partnership with auto firm Rivian – Batteries International
content: Redwood Materials is to recycle scrap and end-of-life EV batteries from US auto firm Rivian as part of an expanded partnership agreement. This new scope of the partnership builds on existing work, announced in April 2026, which includes deploying 10MWh of battery energy storage from repurposed Rivian battery packs at the automaker’s Illinois plant. Redwood, which announced the move on October 16, said it already collects used Rivian EV battery packs through the automaker’s nationwide network of service centres. Redwood evaluates the battery packs for potential re-use in ESS systems used at Rivian’s manufacturing facilities or other locations, or for recycling. Redwood will now also recycle battery scrap generated by Rivian’s operations. JB Straubel, Redwood founder and CEO, said every returned Rivian battery pack was a potential source of domestic grid energy storage in addition to critical materials. “Redwood’s ability to integrate and redeploy Rivian batteries with our technology is an opportunity to enable fast, flexible and more cost-efficient energy storage. As the demand and cost for energy keeps rising, working with companies like Rivian is how we help meet these challenges.” In October 2025, Redwood closed a $350 million funding round to accelerate the firm’s creation of a new generation of US-made energy storage systems. Redwood has also signed a non-binding memorandum of understanding with General Motors to speed up deployment of ESS using both new US-manufactured batteries from GM and second-life battery packs from GM’s electric vehicles. Batteries International reported earlier this year that former Tesla chief financial officer, Deepak Ahuja, was joining Redwood as CFO. title: VIP visit marks GS Yuasa’s 45-year manufacturing milestone in Wales – Batteries International
content: GS Yuasa has celebrated 45 years of manufacturing in Wales with a visit to its Ebbw Vale factory by Japan’s ambassador to the UK. Hiroshi Suzuki and other dignitaries toured the factory on October 14, where the ambassador highlighted the Japan-headquartered company’s long-standing investment, innovative battery technology and commitment to sustainability. GS Yuasa Battery Manufacturing UK, established in 1981, has produced more than 90 million batteries, with over 60% of its products exported, primarily to European markets. Ebbw Vale manufactures Yuasa industrial batteries that provide backup power for critical applications including data centres, UPS systems, telecoms and emergency infrastructure. Latest innovations at the site include Yuasa’s advanced SWL+ range, which uses hybrid pure-lead technology and the firm’s HT Element X Alloy — which Yuasa said delivers high-rate performance and a design life of up to 15 years, incorporating recycled materials and designed to be 98% recyclable. On sustainability, the visit showcased Yuasa’s investment in more sustainable manufacturing including almost 3,000 solar panels on site, wind energy generation and an innovative dual-chemistry battery energy storage system to increase use of renewable energy and reduce reliance on externally supplied electricity. The hybrid lead acid and lithium ion BESS, unveiled in 2017, was deployed in the UK to deliver peak shifting services through a partnership that includes the Infinite Group, University of Sheffield, Innovate UK and GS Yuasa. Shaun Gardner, MD of GS Yuasa Battery Manufacturing UK, said: “By combining Japanese engineering excellence with Welsh manufacturing expertise, we continue to develop innovative products such as SWL+ while investing in more sustainable production. We’re proud of our heritage and remain firmly committed to the future of battery manufacturing in South Wales.” Earlier this year, GS Yuasa revealed plans to expand traction battery operations and its distribution network across European markets. title: EU Battery Passport Drives Cell-Level Traceability
content:
Battery Management Systems
Lithium-Ion Batteries
Design & Manufacturing
Industry Trends
See how Dukosi and STMicroelectronics collaborate on a secure cell-to-cloud platform to help OEMs meet EU Battery Passport rules with scalable, cell-level traceability.
October 23, 2026
6 Min Read
A battery demonstrator showing prismatic cells, each fitted with a Dukosi DK8102 Cell Monitor.
Electrification continues to scale across renewable energy storage, marine, aerospace, industrial, and automotive applications. While headlines often focus on battery performance or charging speeds, sustainability regulations are taking effect and driving the need for greater lifetime traceability.
Coming into force in 2027, the
EU Battery Regulation
will require digital battery passports for batteries over 2 kWh, setting clear expectations for how data is captured, retained, and shared across the full lifecycle of the battery.
For OEMs, this goes beyond a simple compliance exercise. It introduces requirements to manage structured, secure, and persistent data from battery manufacture through operation and eventual recycling, spanning both static information, such as origin and composition, and dynamic data, such as performance and usage history. The question is how to meet battery passport requirements without adding disproportionate integration burden or complexity to already demanding system designs.
Related:
Your Vehicle Battery Doesn't Know What an Hour Is
Battery passport as an engineering challenge
A compliant battery passport must maintain accurate, trustworthy data throughout the battery’s lifecycle. Approaches that link a battery pack to a cloud database through a serial number or QR code marking can provide traceability at pack-level, but that linkage weakens as soon as the battery enters service, repair, reuse, or end-of-life pathways. For OEMs, the immediate challenge is not only future recycling, but maintaining confidence in the data that supports maintenance, warranty, supply-chain verification, and long-term asset value.
This becomes significantly more difficult when data is held only at pack level. As batteries are serviced, reconfigured, or assessed for second-life use, the connection between the physical asset and its operational history can become fragmented, limiting the intelligence available to OEMs, operators, and service partners. Alternatively, persistent data tied directly to each cell provides a stronger foundation for provenance, diagnostics, authenticated servicing, and sustainability commitments, while also supporting future reuse and recycling at a more granular level.
Capturing high-fidelity data at the cell level, rather than inferring it at the module or pack level
Ensuring that data persists through disassembly, repurposing/reuse, and recycling
Providing secure authentication and data integrity across the system
Integrating these capabilities without introducing additional system complexity or cost
While cell-level architectures offer a clear pathway to meeting these challenges, many OEMs are still working to establish the foundations required for battery passport compliance at the pack level.
A demonstration of a secure, scalable battery passport
Battery OEMs want to achieve cost-effective, regulatory-ready status, which means having scalability and flexibility to accommodate design freedom, without introducing additional complexity. Proven solutions are preferred because they reduce development risk.
As requirements expand to include lifecycle traceability, secure authentication, and persistent data, the integration burden increases, particularly when it must be delivered within existing development timelines. This is compounded by the scale of data involved, with standards such as DIN DKE SPEC 99100 (EU Battery Passport) requiring persistent logging of over 100 lifecycle and operational parameters per battery.
To tackle this complex challenge, Dukosi and ST have developed a complete battery management reference platform that includes a secure cell-to-cloud battery passport with the complementary Cell Passport on-chip storage offered by Dukosi. The reference platform combines the following:
The Dukosi Cell Monitoring System (DKCMS), a novel smart cell architecture that embeds data storage directly on each cell,.
An STMicroelectronics STM32H533 MCU (acting as BMU host) and STSAFE-A120 secure element.
The individual cell data and battery data are designed to be accessible remotely via secure cloud service, supporting regulatory requirements. Communication between system hub and cells is achieved using Dukosi’s C-SynQ communication protocol and near field RF via a single bus antenna, removing the need for traditional wiring harnesses and simplifying the mechanical and electrical design of the battery, while ensuring synchronous data capture from all cells and deterministic transmission to the BMU host, which are essential for accurate battery management calculations.
A block diagram of Dukosi and ST demonstrator. Courtesy of Dukosi.
The demonstrator module from Dukosi and ST is based on a single battery module containing 16 cells, each fitted with a DK8102 Cell Monitor (CM). These monitors each allow measurement of voltage and temperature and have integrated non-volatile data storage on each cell, communicating synchronously with a DK8202 System Hub through a single contactless bus antenna built into the module housing, which streamlines battery design and manufacturing.
Each Cell Monitor allows storage of both static and dynamic data at the point of origin, including identity, manufacturing data, and operational history, remaining associated with the physical cell throughout its lifecycle, even if the battery is re-manufactured or the cells are repurposed. The demonstrator module simulates charge and discharge cycles, overvoltage events, and controlled temperature variations to show how their effects can be observed and recorded.
System operation: Data capture, validation, and traceability
In the demonstrator, dynamic operating conditions are actively introduced to generate representative battery passport data. One designated cell includes an internal heater that can be user-controlled to create variable temperature conditions, while variable voltage is applied across the module to simulate charge and discharge cycles as well as overvoltage events. These operating conditions form part of the dynamic dataset within the battery passport and, together with static data such as identity and manufacturing information, are written to the non-volatile memory of each Cell Monitor, remaining associated with the physical cell throughout its lifecycle.
Each Cell Monitor carries a unique ID, which is securely registered and validated through the STSAFE-A120, ensuring that both identity and associated data are protected against tampering or duplication. Data from the cell network is aggregated by the DK8202 System Hub and passed via SPI to the STM32H533 MCU, where the secure element provides authentication and encryption before any data is exchanged beyond the battery system.
The Dukosi and ST demonstrator module facilitates EU Battery Passport readiness via cell-to-cloud secure data storage and access. Courtesy of Dukosi.
This linkage between cell identity and stored data enables persistent, verifiable traceability required for the EU Battery Passport, while avoiding the need to manage identity, data storage, and security as separate subsystems. For OEMs, this reduces the integration effort to meet EU Battery Passport requirements, while for operators it provides a consistent view of asset condition and provenance across the battery lifecycle.
The same architecture supports lifecycle events such as supply chain security, maintenance, and repair. When an individual cell is removed and replaced, the system detects a mismatch in the new cell’s identity on the network, flags a potential tampering event, and restricts access to system data and operation until an authorization process is completed.
The EU Battery Passport is arriving at a point where the industry needs more than regulatory readiness. OEMs, operators, and recyclers need trusted battery data that can support maintenance, warranty decisions, asset valuation, second-life assessment, and end-of-life recovery without adding complexity to already demanding system designs.
For OEMs and battery operators, the challenge is delivering this capability without adding significant cost, development time, or system complexity. This is particularly important in automotive markets, but the same pressure applies across industrial electrification, marine, aerospace, and battery energy storage systems, where scalability, reliability, and cost remain critical.
The demonstrator module developed by Dukosi and STMicroelectronics shows how this can be addressed through native architecture rather than a layer of additional integration burden. By combining cell-level monitoring, contactless communication, secure authentication, and cell-to-cloud data handling, it provides both EU Battery Passport readiness and granular cell-level traceability.
As regulation moves from definition to implementation, the differentiator will be how effectively battery systems can capture, secure, and retain trusted data at scale. Architectures that simplify integration while keeping data tied to the cell will be central to translating OEM compliance into operational and commercial value.

title: ABB Brings Physical AI to Fashion Logistics
content:
ABB Brings Physical AI to Fashion Logistics
Prioritise Us
on Google
ABB Robotics has launched its first end-to-end, vision-based industrial-grade physical AI solution, integrating AI Robot Trainer into its Fashion Inductor module for automated fashion logistics. Credit: ABB Robotics
ABB Robotics Managing Director Craig McDonnell explains how AI Robot Trainer is changing fashion logistics automation
ABB Robotics has launched its first end-to-end, vision-based industrial-grade physical AI solution, integrating AI Robot Trainer into its Fashion Inductor module for automated fashion logistics.
The combined solution is designed to help system integrators deploy, scale and continuously optimise robotic sorting applications with less engineering effort and lower project risk. ABB says the upgrade can reduce engineering and commissioning effort by up to 75% while supporting throughput of up to 1,300 items per hour per cell and picking accuracy targets above 99.5%.
The launch coincides with rapid
in global shipments of professional service robotics, according to the International Federation of Robotics (IFR), highlighting a major shift toward commercial automation across global supply chains.
Supply Chain Digital has reported on rising
interest
in deploying robots in fashion supply chains.
"Fashion Inductor is the first step in our broader rollout of vision-based Physical AI, as we continue developing robots that are increasingly autonomous, versatile and able to adapt to the world around them,” says Craig McDonnell, Managing Director, Business Line Industries, ABB Robotics.
The challenges of fashion logistics
Fashion logistics is difficult to automate because garments, packaging, product presentation and operating conditions can change continuously. The upgraded Fashion Inductor is designed for this variability, using application-specific vision technology, AI-powered Automatic Path Planning and ABB’s robot-control platforms.
AI Robot Trainer adds pre-trained fashion-specific vision models, application tools and rapid retraining capabilities. This allows system integrators to adapt applications as product ranges and operating requirements change without relying on specialist AI expertise.
ABB describes the system as a lifecycle-managed physical AI solution rather than a one-time automation deployment. Models can be developed, deployed, monitored and improved as the robotic cell encounters new products and operating conditions.
“What excites me most is what this represents beyond one application. Fashion Inductor is the first step in our broader rollout of vision-based Physical AI, as we continue developing robots that are increasingly autonomous, versatile and able to adapt to the world around them,” says Craig McDonnell, Managing Director, Business Line Industries, ABB Robotics.
“Fashion logistics is exactly the kind of environment where Physical AI can make a real difference. Products, packaging and operating conditions are constantly changing, demanding automation that can adapt with them,” Craig adds.
Craig, McDonnell, Managing Director, Business Line Industries, ABB Robotics
AI Robot Trainer reduces deployment effort
The principal commercial benefit of AI Robot Trainer is a reduction in the work required to engineer and commission a robotic cell. ABB says the technology can reduce that effort by up to 75%.
The platform combines pre-trained models with application-specific tools and cell-level retraining. This is intended to reduce the time required to teach robots how to identify and handle changing fashion products.
Key capabilities include: pre-trained fashion vision models for faster application deployment; rapid AI retraining for new products, packaging and operating conditions; application-specific tools for system integrators; closed-loop performance monitoring throughout the robot lifecycle; anomaly identification based on real production performance; new training-data generation when the system encounters changing conditions; model redeployment to improve the physical robot’s performance; and reduced reliance on specialist AI expertise.
The 75% figure is an ABB-reported potential reduction in engineering and commissioning effort. Actual results will depend on application complexity, cell configuration, integration requirements and operating conditions.
Digital twin connects software and hardware
The upgraded Fashion Inductor also includes a new digital twin. ABB says the new digital twin replicates the module software and connects the Application Controller Platform, Automatic Path Planning, AI Robot Trainer and RobotStudio.
The digital twin is intended to accelerate commissioning and provide more flexibility during system set-up. It can also support the integration of third-party components, including grippers, within the wider robotic cell.
RobotStudio provides the virtual environment for design, simulation and validation. The OmniCore robot controller acts as the execution layer during production.
Continuous optimisation for changing products
Traditional robotic systems can require substantial re-engineering when products, packaging or handling requirements change. ABB’s approach is designed to make model improvement part of normal system operation.
AI Robot Trainer supports a continuous closed-loop workflow that monitors performance, identifies anomalies, generates additional training data and deploys updated models back to the physical robot.
This matters in fashion logistics because the operating environment is not static. Product ranges can change frequently, garments may arrive in different orientations and packaging formats can vary. A vision-based system must therefore respond to more than a fixed set of production conditions.
ABB’s Fashion Inductor targets:
Throughput: Up to 1,300 items per hour per cell
Picking accuracy: Above 99.5%
Engineering and commissioning: Up to 75% less effort, according to ABB
Primary application: Fashion and apparel logistics
Technology approach: Vision-based physical AI
AI model strategy: Pre-trained models with cell-specific retraining
Deployment model: Digital twin-supported commissioning
Control architecture: RobotStudio and OmniCore
The published throughput and accuracy figures are company targets and should not be interpreted as guaranteed performance across every deployment.
ABB expands physical AI roadmap
Fashion Inductor is the first step in ABB Robotics’ broader rollout of vision-based physical AI. The company says the same AI Robot Trainer-powered approach will expand across additional vision-based applications through the first quarter of 2027.
ABB links this development to its work on increasingly autonomous and versatile robotics, referred to by the company as AVR. The objective is to enable robots to operate effectively in more variable environments while reducing the specialist knowledge required to deploy and maintain them.
For system integrators, the combination of pre-trained models, digital simulation, automated path planning and continuous retraining could shorten deployment cycles and make AI-powered robotic applications easier to scale. The main test will be whether these benefits translate consistently across different customer sites, product mixes and third-party equipment configurations.
Meet the partners

Headquarters: Zurich, Switzerland
ABB is a global technology leader in electrification and automation, driving software-integrated engineering solutions to optimize manufacturing and robotics performance. ABB is the parent technology company behind the robotics portfolio. Its wider automation capabilities provide the corporate and engineering foundation for ABB Robotics’ physical-AI, robot-control and simulation platforms.
ABB Robotics
President: Marc Segura
Headquarters: Zurich, Switzerland
ABB Robotics developed Fashion Inductor and AI Robot Trainer, combining vision, robotic motion, automatic path planning and lifecycle-based AI optimisation for fashion logistics applications.

title: Pigment Raises $250m for Enterprise Planning Capabilities
content:
Pigment Raises $250m for Enterprise Planning Capabilities
Prioritise Us
on Google
Pigment is helping organisations with their enterprise planning. Credit: Getty Images
Pigment is increasing capabilities for enterprise planning, followed by a successful round of Series E funding, CEO of Pigment, Eléonore Crespo explains
Pigment, an AI-powered planning platform, has just received a major sum in Series E funding, allowing it to grow its capabilities in supporting industry leaders.
AI is driving the future of supply chains, but each industry has its own specific issue to face.
Pigment, therefore, is working to
define how AI can be used within business planning
and performance management – and this new funding is helping it unlock new possibilities.
Supply chain volatility
Pigment was founded in 2019 in order to improve how businesses plan,
make decisions and drive growth
. For any large business, it can be a difficult task to plan and adapt to change, even without the challenges of the last few years.
Solutions needed to be easy to use but also powerful enough to cope with the ongoing challenges within the market. When Eléonore Crespo and Romain Niccoli founded Pigment, the goal was – and still is – to build a unified enterprise platform with the fastest time to value, for any business user.
This means that businesses will be able to withstand any challenge, leaving employees to focus on meaningful work rather than reactive firefighting. As a result, businesses can prioritise growth and innovation initiatives and can explore a more sustainable operation.
The role of AI is as a driving force, helping leaders to navigate large sums of data and make sense of it all. In
today’s era of ongoing volatility
and uncertainty, leaders need to be able to adapt in order to stay resilient. The aim of Pigment is to help them do exactly that.
At a glance
Pigment raised US$250m in Series E funding
The company has been valued at US$2.3bn
85% of new metrics in Pigment are created by an agent
In 2026, Pigment surpassed US$100m in Annual Recurring Revenue
Pigment has shipped more than 50 AI capabilities over the past nine months
Funding capabilities
Pigment is now celebrating a successful round of funding, having raised US$250m as it continues to strive for growth. The funding, led by Scaleup Europe Fund, with participation from WiL, alongside existing investors Greenoaks, ICONIQ, IVP and Meritech, as well as a planned investment from NVIDIA.
“I am so excited to announce our US$250m Series E, valuing us at US$2.3bn,” says Eléonore Crespo, Co-Founder and Co-CEO of Pigment.
Éléonore Crespo, CEO and Co-founder of Pigment
“This capital is going to help us change the game for enterprise planning. Imagine a planning cycle that runs end to end on its own. Agents build the forecast, run the scenarios, build the plan and execute on its own within the guardrails that your team sets, and you get your time back to focus on what’s most critical: the strategy. That’s autonomous planning, and it's happening now.”
The funds provide a boost for the company, helping to drive one of the biggest shifts that planning has ever seen. The planning cycle running on its own means that the team can work on its own strategy. Autonomous planning is a significant time saver, and as 85% of new metrics in Pigment are already created by an agent, the route to efficiency is already looking strong.
Plans for growth
Pigment is used by
organisations such as Unilever, Snowflake
, Siemens and Anthropic, demonstrating its capabilities in transforming planning. Through AI, Pigment is helping to build the forecast, run scenarios and execute plans, operating within the guardrails each company has set.
Pigment is growing significantly, working with innovations and
developing new agents
in order to drive transformation within its clients’ planning capabilities. In the last five months, Pigment has shipped more than 50 AI capabilities, using plain-language instructions to build planning models and custom interfaces.
At present, 85% of new metrics on the Pigment software are created by an agent. It connects directly with other AI solutions, integrating into pre-existing tools. This means that organisations do not need to worry about a framework overhaul, resulting in greater efficiency, more cost savings and faster time-to-value than if using other solutions.
Much of the latest funding will go into expanding Pigment’s Graphite engine. Graphite is its underlying infrastructure, helping the team challenge the boundaries of enterprise planning. The goal is to accelerate R&D and its engineering team in order to develop more solutions and help a wider client base.
This capital is going to help us change the game for enterprise planning.
Eléonore Crespo, Co-Founder and Co-CEO of Pigment
Pigment is helping organisations plan more efficiently. Credit: Pigment
Key Companies

HQ: Paris, Île-de-France
Pigment is a cloud-based business planning platform that helps organizations with financial planning, analysis, and strategic decision-making. Founded in 2019, the company provides enterprise performance management software that enables real-time collaboration across finance, sales, and operations teams. Pigment has raised significant venture capital funding and serves major global enterprises seeking to modernize their planning processes with flexible, scalable solutions.

The company's chips are essential for machine learning, deep learning, and generative AI systems. NVIDIA has become one of the world's most valuable companies, experiencing explosive growth driven by AI demand.
Unilever

Unilever is a multinational consumer goods corporation producing food, beverages, cleaning agents, and personal care products. With origins dating to the 1890s, Unilever owns over 400 brands including Dove, Axe, Lipton, Hellmann's, and Ben & Jerry's. The company operates in more than 190 countries, employing approximately 127,000 people. Unilever emphasizes sustainability initiatives and serves billions of consumers daily with household-name products.
Snowflake

HQ: California, USA
Snowflake is a cloud-based data warehousing company that enables organizations to store, manage, and analyze data across multiple clouds. Founded in 2012, Snowflake went public in 2020 in one of the largest software IPOs ever. The platform allows businesses to break down data silos and share information securely. Snowflake serves thousands of customers globally, providing scalable solutions for data engineering, science, and analytics.

Siemens is a global technology powerhouse focusing on industry, infrastructure, transport, and healthcare. Founded in 1847, the company has evolved into a leader in industrial automation, digitalization, and smart infrastructure. The company develops solutions for sustainable energy, intelligent buildings, efficient factories, and modern transportation systems, driving innovation across multiple sectors.

title: How Teradyne, NVIDIA & Sereact Automate Retail Returns
content:
How Teradyne, NVIDIA & Sereact Automate Retail Returns
Prioritise Us
on Google
he company has deployed more than 100,000 robot systems in operational environments across manufacturing, logistics and retail sectors. Credit: Teradyne
Teradyne and Sereact deploy NVIDIA-powered AI vision systems on automated Universal Robots arms, enabling autonomous handling for retail returns
A collaboration between
Teradyne Robotics
and Sereact could reshape how retailers and logistics operators handle unstructured tasks.
The partnership centres on deploying Sereact's Cortex platform, a Vision-Language-Action model, onto robot arms manufactured by
Universal Robots
. Teradyne owns both Universal Robots and Mobile Industrial Robots.
Hundreds of dual-arm robot systems have already shipped to customer sites across Europe. The deployments process returned fashion items at Zalando fulfilment centres in Greven, Germany, and Świebodzin, Poland. CEVA Logistics collaborates on the installations.
The technology addresses a longstanding challenge in
warehouse automation
: handling items with unpredictable shapes, materials and packaging.
“Returns are one of the hardest jobs in logistics," says
Dr. Ralf Gulde
, CEO and Co-Founder of Sereact. "Items differ in shape, orientation and packaging, and the mix changes continuously.
"That is exactly what Cortex is built to handle on the Universal Robots platform.
installations planned for North American fulfilment centres in 2027. Credit: Teradyne
Cortex runs on robot arms
Sereact's Cortex model enables robots to grasp, identify and handle objects they have never encountered before. The system operates on robot arms from the Universal Robots Gen 7 platform, which launched in September.
The deployment addresses a critical operational challenge in ecommerce logistics. Returns processing typically requires manual inspection and sorting because items arrive in unpredictable conditions and packaging. Traditional automation struggles with this variability, but the AI-powered systems adapt to different scenarios without reprogramming.
The integration of Cortex with Universal Robots hardware creates a system capable of adapting to changing product mixes in real time. This flexibility proves particularly valuable in retail returns processing, where items arrive in varied conditions and packaging states.
Anders Billesø Beck, VP AI Robotics Products at Universal Robots, told AI Magazine: "This partnership pairs Sereact's AI 'brain' with the Universal Robots platform and the industrial expertise Universal Robots has built through more than 100,000 deployments in real production."
Anders Billesø Beck Headshot
Anders added: "That combination opens up tasks that were out of reach for automation, from returns handling to items a robot has never seen before."
Jacob Pascual Pape, Chief Commercial Officer of Teradyne Robotics, says: "Physical AI only matters when it performs in real-world operations, and that is where Universal Robots has always been at home."
NVIDIA frameworks power AI training
Cortex is trained in NVIDIA Isaac Sim, an open simulation framework, using NVIDIA Cosmos open world models. Post-training uses reinforcement learning via the NVIDIA Isaac Lab framework. Each model undergoes benchmarking on Teradyne Robotics hardware before deployment.
At deployment, Cortex runs on NVIDIA Jetson Thor at cell level where inference must happen at line speed. Site-level development, validation and model updates use NVIDIA DGX Spark. Universal Robots and Mobile Industrial Robots already integrate NVIDIA computing across their product ranges.
The companies marked the collaboration with a joint demonstration at NVIDIA GTC Berlin 2026.
Teradyne Robotics uses NVIDIA computing across its Universal Robots and Mobile Industrial Robots product ranges. Credit: Teradyne
NVIDIA frameworks power AI training
Cortex is trained in NVIDIA Isaac Sim, an open simulation framework, using NVIDIA Cosmos open world models. Post-training uses reinforcement learning via the NVIDIA Isaac Lab framework. Each model undergoes benchmarking on Teradyne Robotics hardware before deployment.
Site-level development, validation and model updates use NVIDIA DGX Spark.
At deployment, Cortex runs on NVIDIA Jetson Thor at cell level where inference must happen at line speed. This performance level reduces sorting times for facilities that process high volumes of mixed inventory, particularly during returns-heavy periods following seasonal sales events.
The edge computing architecture allows the systems to operate reliably in
warehouse environments
where network connectivity may be intermittent. Local processing also reduces latency in robotic decision-making, enabling faster cycle times for high-throughput operations.
Universal Robots and Mobile Industrial Robots already integrate NVIDIA computing across their product ranges. The companies marked the collaboration with a joint demonstration at NVIDIA GTC Berlin 2026.
Sereact targets global expansion
Sereact was founded in Stuttgart by Dr Ralf Gulde and Marc Tuscher. According to the company, it raised a US$116m Series B in 2026. The firm develops software that allows robots to work with mixed goods, unknown items and varied packaging.
Dr Gulde says: "Partnering with Teradyne Robotics and its global distribution and integrator network helps us bring that one brain to their customers around the world, accelerating the abilities of retailers and logistics providers to adopt AI-powered automation across their operations."
Jacob explains that the product is being actively deployed at customer sites. He adds: "Our robots are built for the AI era: open, connected and proven through more than 100,000 industrial deployments. That is why Sereact has chosen our platform."
The partnership targets retailers and logistics providers seeking to automate returns handling and piece-picking operations. According to the companies, the robots now autonomously process returned fashion items at Zalando fulfilment centres. Teradyne Robotics collaborates with partners including Siemens, NVIDIA and Bright Machines on broader factory automation initiatives.

Siemens works with Universal Robots and MiR to integrate collaborative robotics into factory automation through TIA Portal environments.
NVIDIA provides edge computing capabiilities and simulation platforms that support AI deployment across Teradyne's robotics portfolio.
Bright Machines
Bright Machines collaborates with Teradyne to implement collaborative robots and automated testing solutions in AI-driven microfactories.

title: Primark: Transforming Supply Chain Decision-Making
content:
Primark: Transforming Supply Chain Decision-Making
Prioritise Us
on Google
Primark is investing in digital twin technology to increase its operational efficiency. Credit: Primark
Retailer Primark has selected Kallikor to transform supply chain decision-making in order to run more efficiently, Jack O’Connell, CEO of Kallikor explains
Affordable retailer Primark is undertaking a supply chain transformation in the form of simulations.
The company will be
making use of digital twins
in order to test new solutions and navigate today’s market.
To do so, the company has chosen Kallikor, the supply chain network design platform, to help the organisation to test and validate changes.
Supply chain transformation
Since it was founded in 1969, Primark has grown into an international fashion retailer, with more than 500 stores across Europe, the US and the Middle East. As a high-street name, the company is trusted by millions of shoppers every week to help with every day essentials and the latest trends. Alongside this, it is celebrated for its affordability, ensuring it is accessible to as many customers as possible.
The company is undertaking a mission of making affordable clothes last longer and exist more sustainably,
working to become more circular
in its operations, with reduced waste and emissions, as well as protecting the lives of those making the clothes.
Facing new standards and a high demand, Primark is making changes to its supply chain decision-making process, aiming for greater efficiency and resilience. By working with Kallikor and its simulation-led approach, Primark will see new strength in how it tests and validates operational and capital changes before implementation.
“As Primark continues to grow across markets, ensuring our supply chain is designed to
support that ambition is critical
,” explains Adam Hoccom, Director of Supply Chain at Primark.
Primark is undergoing a period of growth and requires confident decision-making | opening of the Cremona store in July 2026. Credit: Primark
“A key part of that is making sure our distribution centres operate efficiently while remaining aligned to store needs. Working with Kallikor allows us to test and compare different operating configurations – from layout and flow changes within sites to broader network considerations – before we commit capital spend.
“This gives us greater confidence in the choices we make and how they will perform in practice, strengthening our ability to innovate and make well-informed decisions as we evolve our network.”
At a glance
Primark has more than 500 stores across 19 countries
Millions of shoppers visit Primark every week
Kallikor helps deliver an average of US$14.2m in identified value within six months of engagement
According to Kallikor, only 19% of major retail supply chain decisions are delivered as intended
90% of leaders say major decisions carry reputational risk, according to Kallikor
Simulation-led approach
At the beginning of the partnership, Kallikor will
create digital twins
of Primark’s distribution centres, which means teams can test alternative solutions before they implement them. Through comparing simulated scenarios, Primark can find more efficient approaches to its operations without impacting sales.
When a company of Primark’s scale makes a major transformation, it runs the risk of impacting customer service or downstream cost. By running simulations, Primark can understand what works without creating operational impacts across the company. This means lower risk for a higher potential reward.
The operational flow will be looked at in detail, giving Primark the ability to explore labour constraints and throughput variability. By doing so in a simulation, Primark can see how these changes will perform in advance, allowing the company to
evaluate the cost-effectiveness
of the change and whether it is worth the overhaul.
Teams are able to continuously test solutions using a singular validated model, allowing for a range of strategic questions and solutions as the supply chain continues to evolve. This means the model is constantly learning and Primark is keeping pace with modern challenges and demands.
“For a retailer of Primark’s scale, the decisions that matter most are the big, hard-to-reverse ones: where to add capacity, how to serve customers in new ways, how to run more efficiently,” Jack O’Connell, CEO & Co-Founder of Kallikor tells Supply Chain Digital.
Jack O’Connell, CEO & Co-Founder of Kallikor
“Our partnership gives Primark a way to test those decisions against how its operations actually run, using a simulation built from the detail of individual sites, shifts and processes. That means seeing the full consequence of a change before committing to it: what it costs across the operation, where it puts pressure on service, and how well the network copes when volumes spike or a site is disrupted.
“And because the model is kept up to date as the business changes, Primark can keep using it for every major decision that follows. The result is big calls made with evidence a leadership team can stand behind.”
Scaling technology
Primark teams will be using simulation and AI-enabled scenario exploration in order to run and compare multiple operating futures side-by-side. This allows them to examine trade-offs across cost, service, capacity and risk.
Through this, decisions can be made with greater confidence and clarity, with a system-wide evidence base that supports cross-functional alignment.
The initial scenarios will be run to focus on distribution centre configuration, but it can be reused as new demands arise. Through this, teams can test automation pathways, capital investments and
future growth scenarios
Primark is taking a step towards more evidence-based supply chain decision-making, working to establish growth and investment plans that will be a guaranteed success.
For a retailer of Primark’s scale, the decisions that matter most are the big, hard-to-reverse ones: where to add capacity, how to serve customers in new ways, how to run more efficiently.
Jack O’Connell, CEO & Co-Founder of Kallikor
Key companies

HQ: Dublin, Ireland
Primark is an Irish fast-fashion retailer owned by Associated British Foods, operating over 400 stores across Europe and the United States. Founded in 1969, the company specializes in affordable clothing, accessories, homeware, and beauty products. Known for its "amazing fashion, amazing prices" motto, Primark maintains low costs through efficient supply chains and minimal advertising, instead relying on high-volume sales and prime retail locations to attract budget-conscious shoppers.
Kallikor
CEO: Jack O'Connell
HQ: London, United Kingdom
Kallikor provides a supply chain network design platform that creates digital twin simulations, enabling organizations to test major decisions before implementation. The company models transport flows and sites to bring operational realism to strategic planning. Serving clients including Morrisons, Primark, and B&M, Kallikor typically delivers decision-ready evidence in 4–8 weeks, with an average $14.2M in value identified within six months.

title: Sanofi Invests in Insulin Plant in Frankfurt
content:
Sanofi Invests in Insulin Plant in Frankfurt
Prioritise Us
on Google
Rendering of the new insulin manufacturing facility at Sanofi BioCampus Frankfurt. Credit: Sanofi
Sanofi CEO Belén Garijo outlines how a multi-billion Frankfurt facility will use AI and automation to strengthen Europe’s insulin supply
Sanofi has begun construction of a nearly EUR2bn (US$2.24bn) insulin manufacturing facility at its Frankfurt BioCampus, securing a long-term European production base for human insulin.
Planned to enter full production in 2032, the 36,000-square-metre site will use modern automation, digital systems and
artificial intelligence
manufacturing
and quality operations, replacing an existing older insulin production facility on the same site.
“Millions of people around the world rely on insulin every day, and our commitment to them is for the long term. With this new facility, we are investing in the next generation of insulin manufacturing in Europe, building on more than a century of expertise and a strong industrial footprint in Frankfurt. Maintaining the right conditions for investment and innovation will be essential to Europe’s future competitiveness,” said Belén Garijo
Chief Executive Officer, Sanofi.
Belén Garijo, CEO of Sanofi. Credit: Sanofi.
Sanofi retains insulin manufacturing in Germany
The new facility will be built at Sanofi’s integrated Frankfurt BioCampus. The site covers the insulin value chain from active pharmaceutical ingredient production through filling, device assembly and packaging.
The new plant will occupy an area equivalent to approximately five football fields and is expected to become one of Europe’s largest and most advanced insulin manufacturing facilities once operational.
The new facility is intended to strengthen the company’s ability to maintain supply over the long term as global demand changes. Sanofi says more than 500 million people worldwide live with diabetes, while the number is expected to exceed 800 million by 2050.
The investment therefore has significance beyond Germany. The Frankfurt site will continue to form part of Sanofi’s global insulin supply network, and continue supplying about 80 countries with 20 insulin products.
Sanofi currently supplies insulin to approximately 15 million people in more than 100 countries each year, according to the company.
Without the investment, Sanofi had warned that production of human insulin at its Frankfurt-Höchst site would cease. About 6,500 people work at Sanofi’s Frankfurt site, including more than 4,000 in its insulin operations.
Representatives from Sanofi and regional German politics attended the opening ceremony at Sanofi's Frankfurt BioCampus. Credit: Belén Garijo via LinkedIn
Production planned for 2032
Construction began following the European Commission’s approval in September 2026 of EUR400m (US$448.82m) of public support from the German Federal Government, the State of Hesse and the City of Frankfurt under the European Union’s state-aid framework. Sanofi initially announced a project investment of approximately EUR1.3bn (US$1.46bn) in 2024. The company now describes the total investment in the Frankfurt facility as nearly EUR2bn (US$2.24bn).
The European Commission’s approval of state aid stipulates that the site produces at least 1.1 tonnes of insulin per year at the site through 2042, and retains a reserve of 1.0t of insulin active pharmaceutical ingredients through 2042.
The aid also requires that Sanofi prioritises sales to European Economic Area (EEA) markets in the event that shortages occur.
Frankfurt-Höchst is the only site producing human insulin in the European Economic Area and one of just two insulin production sites in the EU together with a Novartis production facility in Denmark.
Sanofi currently operates an insulin production facility on its Frankfurt campus. Credit: Sanofi
Key facts about the Sanofi's new production facility
Location: The plant is being built at Sanofi’s BioCampus in Frankfurt, Germany.
Footprint: The facility will cover approximately 36,000 square metres.
Production: Full production of insulin active pharmaceutical ingredients is planned for 2032, subject to licensing.
EU support: Germany received European Commission approval for EUR400m (US$448.82m) in state aid.
Annual output: Sanofi must produce at least 1.1 tonnes of insulin annually at the site.
Strategic reserve: The company must hold 1 tonne of insulin active pharmaceutical ingredients at the site through 2042.
Market priority: EEA markets must be prioritised during insulin shortages.
A boost for European pharma manufacturing
The development represents a large-scale investment by Sanofi in pharmaceutical manufacturing capacity in Europe after a sustained series of investments by European-headquartered groups such as AstraZeneca and Bayer in new or planned manufacturing facilities in the US.
The investment by Sanofi will ensure that Germany will remain an export hub for human insulin production and global supply chains until 2042.

Sanofi engages in the research, production, and distribution of pharmaceutical products. It operates through the Biopharma segment, which comprises commercial operations and research, development and production activities relating to the specialty care, general medicines and vaccines franchises plus support and corporate functions, for all geographical territories.

AstraZeneca is a global biopharmaceutical company focused on the discovery, development, and commercialisation of prescription medicines. Its portfolio spans oncology, rare diseases, and biopharmaceuticals, including cardiovascular, renal & metabolism, and respiratory & immunology.

title: Amazon’s Holiday Expansion: New Jobs and Worker Stability
content:
Amazon’s Holiday Expansion: New Jobs and Worker Stability
Prioritise Us
on Google
Amazon is increasing its seasonal staff numbers. Credit: Amazon
Amazon is investing in its future workforce with its expanded holiday hiring and new company benefits, Udit Madan, SVP Worldwide Operations explains
Amazon has opened its seasonal job opportunities, with new benefits being introduced and a clear pathway to long-term employment at the company.
As holiday shopping continues to increase
demand for the ecommerce giant
, Amazon is hiring more people than in previous years.
Alongside that, it is investing in worker wellbeing – protecting employees and developing greater resilience for its future operations.
Logistics expansion
This holiday season, Amazon is hiring more than 300,000 people for
seasonal, part-time and full-time roles
across its US network. These jobs will be available across Amazon’s core operations across the nation, working across fulfilment centers, customer service, driver network, in-store and at locker locations.
As holiday shopping begins to increase, Amazon will be facing greater demand than any other time in the year. Customers will be buying decorations, presents and food and drink online. Already, the platform is releasing deals – its Holiday Beauty Event running from 19th October - 1st November. Events like these help customers shop in advance while saving money, and also ensures Amazon becomes the go-to place for gift purchasing.
With this comes the need for a broader staff base, meeting the rising demand of shoppers while also maintaining the Prime promise of affordable prices and speedy delivery.
“This holiday season, Amazon is hiring over 300,000 people across the US in our core operations — 20% higher than last year, and one of the largest seasonal hiring pushes in the country,” Udit Madan, Senior Vice President, Worldwide Operations at Amazon posts to LinkedIn.
Udit Madan, Senior Vice President, Worldwide Operations at Amazon
“For many, a season here can turn into something more. Every year, people who start with a seasonal job stay and build careers here, becoming trainers, managers and leaders across our network.”
Amazon’s seasonal hiring acts as an opportunity to gain new work experience and
For many, this represents a new opportunity to gain a solid introduction into Amazon’s operations, as Amazon
invests in its future workforce
At a glance
More than 300,000 people will be hired as part of Amazon’s holiday job postings
Seasonal employees working 30+ hours a week will have healthcare coverage from day 1, beginning on January 1, 2027
Seasonal employees will earn an average of US$20/hour
Amazon will be posting new job openings weekly
Many of the employees will stay on for long-term employment
Investments into the workforce
This year, Amazon is introducing increased benefits to its workforce, including more stability and increased pay. In doing so, it is strengthening its supply chain stability and demonstrating investments into the people within the company.
“The holidays are my favorite time of year at Amazon,” explains J. Ofori Agboka, Vice President - People, Experience and Technology at Amazon.
“There’s an energy across our operations network that’s hard to match as our teams come together to deliver for customers during our busiest season. One of the best parts is welcoming so many new teammates into Amazon and, this year, we’re hiring over 300,000 people for seasonal, part-time and full-time roles across our core operations network nationwide.
J. Ofori Agboka, Vice President - People, Experience and Technology at Amazon.
“As we welcome those new teammates, we’re also continuing to invest in the people who make all of this possible and the benefits that matter most to them and their families.”
For several years, Amazon has been offering healthcare support to its regular, full-time employees starting on day one of their contract.
Company benefits
The online retailer is investing in its staff in other ways. It has announced more than US$1.5bn in higher pay for its US core operations workforce. This breaks down to seasonal staff being paid an average of US$20 an hour. Full-time core operations employees now earn a minimum starting wage of US$20 an hour.
The company is also helping paychecks go further – Amazon employees across the US now get a 10% discount on eligible groceries and everyday essentials on Amazon.com and Whole Foods Market online, as well as a 20% discount in Whole Foods Market stores.
Seasonal jobs offer employees an opportunity to earn money,
learn new skills
and work flexible hours. For some, it is a temporary role, but for others it is their start on the Amazon ladder.
Many seasonal employees have become trainers, managers and leaders, nurtured in these roles through various upskilling programmes and training.
As we welcome those new teammates, we’re also continuing to invest in the people who make all of this possible and the benefits that matter most to them and their families.

Founded in 1994, the company employs over 1.5 million people worldwide. Amazon's operations include Prime delivery, Amazon Web Services, and Whole Foods Market. The company invests over $1.5bn annually in US workforce wages, maintaining competitive advantages through operational excellence.
Whole Foods
Acquired by Amazon in 2017 for $13.7bn, Whole Foods Market serves as both a retail subsidiary and integrated fulfillment hub within Amazon's omnichannel supply chain. The grocery chain offers Amazon employees exclusive benefits including 20% in-store discounts and 10% online discounts. Whole Foods locations function as pickup points, delivery hubs, and employment centers, bridging physical and digital retail operations during peak holiday demand.

Volvo EX60 orders top 50,000 as production lags behind
After reporting third-quarter earnings on Friday, Volvo said the EX60 has been “a big success” so far, receiving over 50,000 orders in Europe since production began in April.
However, the company has built only around 5,000 units so far because of “new industrial technology,” Volvo said, such as the EX60’s cell-to-body structural battery design and manufacturing changes required for its new SPA3 platform.
The Swedish automaker admitted that the production ramp-up is “taking longer than planned,” but promised volumes are steadily improving.
Volvo Car’s president and CEO Håkan Samuelsson said the EX60 will be a cornerstone of Volvo’s comeback plan as one of its most profitable models, but warned that the financial impacts will not be realized until volume picks up.
After delivering the first models in Europe this summer, Volvo planned to ramp up production as the EX60 arrived in new markets, including the US.
Volvo EX60 orders reach over 50,000 in Europe (Source: Volvo Cars Q3 2026 earnings)

Automotive News

of SEK -3.7 billion ($373 million) in the third quarter, with its operating profit margin falling to -5.6%.

Volvo is betting on its new SPA3 platform to lower production costs, boost profit margins, and accelerate its push into software-defined vehicles.

title: Tesla cancels Cybertruck in Australia and NZ after 7 years of deposits
content:
Tesla Cybertruck
Fred Lambert
| Oct 23 2026 - 7:35 am PT
Cyberbeast / Source: Tesla.com
Tesla has officially cancelled the Cybertruck for Australia and New Zealand. Reservation holders are getting emails today telling them their orders are void and their deposits will be refunded.
Australians started putting down A$150 to reserve the electric pickup in November 2019. That’s almost seven years of waiting for a truck Tesla now says it won’t build for them.
“Plans… have been discontinued”
The email, which reservation holders started sharing on social media and Reddit this morning, is short.
“After careful consideration, plans to produce Cybertruck for Australia and New Zealand have been discontinued,” Tesla wrote. “As a result, we’re unable to fulfil your reservation and it will be cancelled.”
Tesla says customers will get a full refund for any payments made, with refunds processed within 30 days. As a consolation, the automaker is offering a free one-year subscription to FSD (Supervised) to reservation holders who order a new Model 3 or Model Y instead.
Tesla is trying to convert a dead Cybertruck reservation into a sale of a car it actually builds in right-hand drive.
The emails went out a day after Tesla reported its Q3 2026 earnings.
Seven years of “next year”
Australia wasn’t a small market on paper. A crowdsourced survey of reservations from 2020 put it third behind the US and Canada, with about 3% of all Cybertruck reservations. Tesla never confirmed regional numbers, but by 2023, crowdsourced tracking
put total Cybertruck reservations at around 2 million
Tesla quietly closed the Australian reservation page in May 2022 and replaced it with a “Get updates” button. It didn’t refund anyone at the time. People who had already reserved just kept waiting.
Then in 2024, Tesla shipped a Cybertruck down under for a display tour, and Elon Musk told shareholders that year: “We might be able to certify it for other markets sometime next year.” Next year came and went, and the truck never got a right-hand-drive version.
That’s the core problem. The Cybertruck is built only in left-hand drive. Australia, New Zealand, the UK, and Japan all need right-hand drive, and Australia also requires certification under its own design rules. That’s a big bill for a truck with a truck that is already having demand issues in North America.
The Cybertruck can’t justify the investment
Tesla’s few international Cybertruck launches all share one thing: they’re left-hand-drive markets. Deliveries
started in South Korea late last year and in the UAE in January
, followed by configurators in Saudi Arabia, Qatar, Jordan, and Israel. The truck remains blocked in the EU, mainly for pedestrian safety reasons.
And the volumes don’t support a right-hand-drive program. Tesla delivered just 8,295 “Other Models” in Q3 2026, a category that’s now almost entirely Cybertruck since Model S and Model X production ended.
We estimate Cybertruck sales at 7,000 to 8,000 units last quarter
, roughly a 30,000-per-year pace for a production line Tesla built for 250,000 units annually.
At that rate, no CFO would sign off on re-engineering the truck for two markets that together have about 33 million people.
Electrek’s Take
This was the obvious outcome for a while, and Tesla should have said so years ago.
Taking deposits in 2019 for a truck that was supposed to start at $39,900 was one thing. Closing the order page in 2022 and letting thousands of people sit on refundable deposits for four more years without a word, while the CEO kept dangling “next year,” is another.
To be fair, a lot of Australian reservation holders likely already canceled their pre-orders. The Cybertruck that showed up in 2023 isn’t the one they reserved. It’s more expensive, has less range than promised, and its US sales have collapsed from about 39,000 in 2024 to a fraction of that today. Paying a premium for an import-ready version would have made it even worse value down under.
But it also confirms what we’ve been saying: the Cybertruck is now a niche, mostly American product. Tesla isn’t likely to invest more in it, and the international expansion is just about finding buyers for the existing left-hand-drive trucks.

title: Tesla's $10B solar factory could get 35 years of tax breaks in Texas
content:
Green Energy
tesla solar
Fred Lambert
| Oct 23 2026 - 7:25 am PT
Tesla’s proposed $10 billion “Project Crystal Sun” solar factory in Texas could get up to 35 years of local tax breaks on its equipment, according to the four agreements Fort Bend County commissioners approved on Thursday.
The vote was 4-0. And Tesla still hasn’t committed to building the plant in Texas.
first reported in August
, Tesla applied for a 10-year school property tax limitation under the state’s JETI program, through Lamar CISD and the Texas Comptroller. The plan is a vertically integrated solar plant near Richmond, southwest of Houston, that would make everything from silicon ingots to finished modules, with commercial production targeted for Q1 2029.
Lamar CISD approved the school tax piece in September. The county was next.
On October 22, the commissioners court approved items 25A to 25D on its agenda: a
Chapter 312 tax abatement
Chapter 381 incentive agreement
foreign trade zone agreement
with a payment in lieu of taxes (PILOT), and a
“true up” PILOT agreement
. Interim County Judge Daniel Wong abstained because his engineering firm has worked with Tesla.
Each agreement covers a different slice of Tesla’s tax bill, and together they run for decades.
Years 1 to 10: no county tax on equipment or inventory
The Chapter 312 agreement abates 100% of county property taxes on Tesla’s equipment and other tangible personal property at the plant for 10 tax years. The clock starts in tax year 2029 by default, but Tesla can move it to the first year after production starts, as late as 2031 without needing the county’s approval.
JETI application
splits the $10.1 billion into $1.52 billion of real property and $8.6 billion of personal property, mostly production equipment.
Land and buildings aren’t part of the deal. Anything that isn’t eligible for the abatement, including the land and buildings, stays “fully taxable at all times,” according to the agreement.
Inventory goes through the foreign trade zone deal instead. Tesla’s site would be part of Port Freeport’s Foreign-Trade Zone No. 149, which exempts eligible inventory from local property tax. In exchange for the county not objecting, Tesla agreed to make PILOT payments, set at “zero dollars or 0%” of the forgone taxes for as long as the abatement is in effect.
Years 11 to 30: Tesla gets 90% back
When the abatement ends, the Chapter 381 agreement takes over. Tesla starts paying county taxes on its equipment, and the county pays 90% of them back as an annual grant for 20 years. The county keeps 10% for its general fund.
Inventory follows the same pattern. After the abatement, Tesla’s FTZ payment rises to 10% of the taxes that would otherwise apply.
The 12,000-job bonus
There’s one more lever. If Tesla averages at least 12,000 employees for any two consecutive years during the first decade, the first five years of the rebate period become a 100% grant, and the rebate period stretches from 20 to 25 years.
That pushes the agreement out to Project Year 35. It’s also 2,288 jobs above the 9,712 Tesla says it will create.
What Tesla has to deliver
To keep the tax breaks, Tesla has to start construction by June 30, 2027, begin “regular commercial production of solar cells” by December 31, 2030, and invest $10 billion by the later of December 31, 2031 or two years after production starts. Force majeure and “ERCOT Delay” provisions can extend those dates.
The jobs ramp is 2,500, 5,000, 7,500, then 9,712 employees by the fourth year of operations, with an average compensation of $55 per hour. Tesla gets the full abatement as long as it hits 90% of the headcount target, which is about 8,741 people.
The penalties are mild. Missing a jobs or wage target for one year only costs Tesla that year’s break, and two misses in a row lets the county terminate the agreement. Full recapture of abated taxes, plus a possible 15% penalty if they aren’t repaid within 60 days, is reserved for “Material Defaults” like missing the $10 billion investment, blowing the construction deadlines or abandoning the plant for 12 months.
Under the Chapter 381 deal, grants from earlier years can’t be clawed back for a headcount shortfall.
The county’s floor is small. The true-up agreement only guarantees that Fort Bend collects at least $2 million a year, and 25% of the taxes Tesla pays on its real property, the county’s 10% share and the FTZ payments all count toward that total.
For scale, Tesla’s own consultant, Kroll, estimated in the JETI filing that the project would pay $276.5 million in Fort Bend County general taxes over 38 years without incentives, peaking at $16.2 million in 2030. That estimate lumps land, buildings and equipment together. The equipment portion is the one the county just agreed to give back, for most of those years.
Shopping for the best deal
In its application, it says the economics of the Fort Bend site are “not competitive” with an unnamed site in another state without the JETI limitation and local abatements. The competing state is redacted in a confidential supplement.
None of the documents state a production capacity. The only big number is a quote from Elon Musk at Davos in January, cited in the application: “The SpaceX and Tesla team, both separately, are working to build to 100 GW a year of solar power in the U.S., of manufactured solar power.”
For comparison, Qcells is spending $2.5 billion on its ingot-to-module campus in Cartersville, Georgia, where a 3.5 GW cell line started production this year. Crystal Sun’s budget is four times that.
Tesla has been here before. New York spent $950 million on the Buffalo factory for Tesla’s solar business, and when the solar plans fell apart, Tesla
turned to things other than solar to meet its employment requirements
, including data labeling for Autopilot. Tesla did
announce production of a new solar panel in Buffalo last year
Electrek’s Take
We want this factory to happen. A US plant making its own ingots, wafers, cells and modules would be rare, and it’s one of the few parts of Tesla’s business that still lines up with the mission it used to talk about before its “awesome abundance” pivot based on AI.
But corporate America loves its tax breaks. For 10 years, Tesla pays no county tax on the $8.6 billion of equipment that makes up most of the project. For the next 20, it gets 90% of it back. In return, the county’s guaranteed minimum is $2 million a year, on a $10 billion plant. And Tesla still hasn’t said it’s coming.
That’s how site selection works now. Companies file, collect offers from several states, and the county that bids the most wins. Fort Bend’s economic development director, Carlos Guzman, told ABC13 the county “would’ve been eliminated from consideration” without these agreements. Hard to argue with that, and it’s exactly why these deals keep getting richer.
The protections are thin too. One bad year costs Tesla a year of breaks, and past rebates can’t be clawed back over a headcount shortfall, even though the county’s goal is obviously long-term employment.
Then there’s the equipment.
Reuters reported in March
that Tesla was in talks to buy $2.9 billion of Chinese solar equipment, and its supply chain is already
caught in a patent fight between Chinese suppliers
The state still has to sign off on the school-tax piece. After that, it’s on Tesla. Is it actually building in Texas, or is Fort Bend’s offer just leverage against the other state? From what I’m hearing, Tesla is set on the Houston-area location.
Tesla wants to start making solar panels in Texas by 2029, but you don’t have to wait that long to go solar at home.
